classification.difficultyReason: Choose familiar examples and explain how their sets of possible values illustrate the discrete–continuous distinction.

content.prompt: Outline the differences between discrete and continuous random variables using at least one example.

answer.short: A discrete random variable takes separate, countable values, such as the number of heads in two tosses. A continuous random variable can take any value in an interval, such as the time taken to run a race.
answer.worked: The number of heads in two tosses is discrete because its possible values are $0$, $1$ and $2$. The time taken to run a race is continuous because it can take any value in an interval of possible times.
